summary: A sound rewrite target (8 shapes on 4 of 6 loads, 1.3-2.6x off their floors, and load_inline already has a precedent here), but the stage-1 design as written does not fit H200 shared memory (2 CTAs/SM x a 4 x 32 KB ring plus x staging is 272-320 KB against a 228 KB/SM limit) and leaves qkv_gate with 288 work items on 264 persistent CTAs. Fix both at build time. It is risk high, so it should wait for a check run and not go out as a scored submit.
justification: Target and mechanism: FINDINGS shows that every replaced kernel is the whole of its shape's time (100% of top_kernels). The kernels are pooler _bf16_splitk_kernel at 19.0/19.3 us (floor 14.0), qkv _qkv_splitk_sem_kernel at 11.8/12.0 (floor 7.9), o _pooler_skinny_kernel at 4.6/5.2 (floor 3.5) and the unpooler slice at 4.5/4.6 (floor 1.7/1.8), with effective bandwidth of 1.9-3.65 TB/s. These 8 shapes make up 4 of 5 shapes on decode_1 and verify_1, i.e. 2 of the 6 equally weighted loads, so a 10% kernel gain there moves the headline by about 2-3%. The expected directions match TASK.md: m=16/32/128/256 and the router are untouched, so they should be flat. The MMA plan is right for this layout. The weight [N,K] row-major is the A operand of mma.m16n8k16 .row, and x [m,K] row-major is exactly B .col, so ldmatrix works without a transpose. n8 covers m<=8, and the math is about 1k mma per SM for the pooler, which is negligible under the bandwidth bound. Correctness is low-risk numerically: bf16 weights at their own precision, fp32 accumulation, and a fixed-order split-K sum. One-hot power-of-two rows come out exact. WEAKEST LINK: the premise that bytes in flight are what cap Triton at about 3.5-3.7 TB/s. By Little's law, 4.8 TB/s at roughly 1 us of DRAM latency needs only about 36 KB in flight per SM, and master already has about 128 KB per CTA. The gap to the floor is therefore more plausibly fixed per-launch cost: launch and first-byte ramp, wave quantization, and the serialized split-K reduce tail. For example, 19.0 us for 67.1 MB is about 4.1 TB/s steady state plus about 2.5 us of fixed cost. A CUDA kernel can shave that fixed cost (TMA/cp.async.bulk issue, all bytes issued up front, a tighter reduce), but the 'double the bytes in flight' argument should not be relied on. M2 (pooler <=17.5 us, about 3.85 TB/s) is plausible. M3 (4.2 TB/s, within about 88% of the HBM3e peak including ramp) is a stretch. The unpooler slice (8.4 MB) is latency-bound: 3.2 us is reachable only if the SPLIT_K=16 reduce tail is kept small. DESIGN DEFECTS TO FIX IN STAGE 1: (1) Shared memory. H200 allows 228 KB/SM (227 KB per block). The '>= 32 KB/stage x 4 stages per CTA at 2 CTAs/SM (>= 256 KB in flight per SM)' plan does not fit, and staging x for the whole K-range adds 8 to 32 KB per CTA (the pooler K-chunk of 2048 needs 32 KB). As written, the launch fails with too many resources, or the occupancy silently drops to 1 CTA/SM. Use, for example, 2 CTAs x (3 stages x 24-32 KB) with x staged per stage (8 x BLOCK_K bf16, 2-4 KB) instead of per K-range, or 1 CTA/SM with 8 warps and a 6 x 32 KB ring. Set cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize explicitly. (2) Balance. qkv gives 36 n-tiles x SPLIT_K 8 = 288 items on 264 CTAs, so 24 CTAs run two items and the makespan is about 2x the mean. Pick a decomposition with items <= CTAs (e.g. 36 x 7 with uneven 128-multiple K-chunks, or 36 x 8 = 288 CTAs at 3 per SM if smem allows), or use finer stream-K items (64 rows x 256 K = 1152 units, about 4.4 per CTA). Pooler 64x4, o 128x2 and unpooler 16x16 all give 256 items and are fine. (3) Partials. At m=1, store and reduce only rows < m. Do not move all 8 rows of [SPLIT_K, 8, n] fp32, because at SPLIT_K=16 on the unpooler that is 512 KB of partial traffic against an 8.4 MB weight.
confounders: bf16-shape-gated-triton-winners-combo (landed): this is the incumbent being replaced (pooler/qkv/o at m<=16 and the unpooler slice). The comparison is the intended one, but the m<=8 rows of qkv_gate/pooler/o share prepare()-allocated ws/cnt buffers sized for m<=16. Give the CUDA path its own workspaces and counters so a counter left non-zero by one path cannot corrupt the other, especially in the self-check and warm-up.

unpooler-slice-triton-splitk8-semaphore (folded into the combo): the slice reads W[:1024] in place with row stride 4096. The CUDA kernel must take stride_wn as an argument and must not assume a contiguous [1024, 4096] tensor; otherwise the m=5 unpooler test fails.

bf16-m32-swapab-wgmma-triton (landed) and sglang-gemm-dispatch-parity: there is no shared kernel, but kernel_fn's gate order matters. The new route must sit ahead of the existing m<=16 gates and be limited to 1<=cfg m<=8, with m=9..16 and the m=17..32 swap-AB path left byte-identical, so the 'flat' rows are truly untouched.

router-triton-hilo-fused-control-splitk-all-m and router-hilo-at-m8: no interaction (the router is untouched). The router verify_1/verify_16 rows drifted 0.92-0.94 on byte-identical code in the combo run, so a router row moving here is drift, not this change.
interference: No companions. This is kind: rewrite, judged on the replaced kernels' own time per shape (top_kernels) against the incumbent and the floor, and the prepare() log prints per-layer warm-L2 kernel time and TB/s, which already isolates the kernel from the headline. No landed hypothesis shares a launch sequence or numerical path with the new kernel: it replaces the incumbent outright on disjoint shapes. An ab-revert would only re-measure master. The useful follow-up is stage 2, which should respond to whatever the stage-1 profile shows: (a) cp.async vs cp.async.bulk if bandwidth stalls below 4 TB/s, (b) extending to m=16, and (c) re-baselining against bf16-m16-swapab-wgmma-extend if that lands first, since it targets the same m=1/m=8 shapes with Triton wgmma.
rules_flags: load_inline is allowed (precedent: muse_attention_decode full-decode-cuda-gather-splitkv, compiled at import in 41 s and passed the checker). Compile time counts against the 10-minute run limit. Keep one translation unit with functions= bindings and no extra headers, and do not use a build or cache directory outside the run's own temp dir (no cross-run caching).

CUDA graph capture: launch on at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream(), never the legacy default stream. Do not call cudaDeviceSynchronize or cudaStreamSynchronize in the wrapper. C10_CUDA_KERNEL_LAUNCH_CHECK / cudaGetLastError are fine. Allocate the output with torch::empty, or torch.empty on the Python side, and never cudaMalloc in the launch path.

The enable/disable flag set by the self-check must be computed once in prepare() from synthetic data. It is a constant of state, never derived from data, which is consistent with the rules as written.
Weights are read unchanged as bf16 (no repack needed). Any swizzled repack must be a lossless bf16 permutation done in prepare().

Not a rules problem but a test-risk one: an illegal-address fault in the new kernel is sticky and cannot be caught by the Python fallback. The self-check protects against wrong answers, not against a crash. Bounds-check the unpooler stride and the m<8 B-column zero-fill carefully.
open_questions: Which smem plan will be built, given that 2 CTAs/SM x 4 x 32 KB plus x does not fit 228 KB/SM? Prefer x staged per stage and 3 stages, or 1 CTA/SM with a deeper ring. Print the achieved occupancy (cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor) in prepare().
qkv decomposition: 288 items on 264 CTAs gives a 2x tail. Which split will be used instead?

Self-check coverage: it should run every m in 1..8 for every layer, call twice in a row (a counter-reset bug shows only on the second launch), include a one-hot power-of-two row (must be exact), and apply a per-row bound (<= 5x the 1e-3 rel-L2 bound) as well as the global rel L2. A wrong token column at one m would slip under a whole-matrix 1e-3.
Should the self-check reference be fp32 (x.float() @ W.float().T) rather than bf16 cuBLAS, so that the 1e-3 threshold measures the kernel and not cuBLAS's own rounding?
Scheduling: risk is high and today's bf16 checks are spent. Per the standing policy (DECISIONS 2026-10-24T164610Z), this should wait for the check reset rather than go out as a scored submit.
If bf16-m16-swapab-wgmma-extend lands first, the m=1/m=8 incumbent changes to Triton wgmma swap-AB. Rebase onto it and compare against its kernel times.
